claims.text: Equiatomic Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Cu nanoparticles have high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy slows atomic diffusion in equiatomic Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Cu nanoparticles.
Slower atomic diffusion suppresses phase segregation in these nanoparticles.
Increasing the Cu content by 10–15% lowers the configurational-entropy barrier.
Lowering the configurational-entropy barrier through Cu enrichment promotes atomic diffusion at high temperature.
Enhanced diffusion in Cu-enriched nanoparticles promotes Cu segregation.
Cu enrichment can alter atomic-size mismatch and surface-energy contributions to phase behavior.
Equiatomic Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Cu nanoparticles will maintain greater structural and chemical homogeneity during thermal exposure than Cu-enriched nanoparticles.
Cu-enriched Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Cu nanoparticles will form Cu-rich clusters or precipitates during thermal exposure.
The proposed behavior applies within 773–1173 K under catalytic conditions and 473–1923 K under thermoelectric conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to systems with substantially different elemental combinations.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to non-equiatomic starting conditions.

contradictions.description: The experiment and central prediction explicitly concern a non-equiatomic, Cu-enriched starting composition, but the boundary statement says the hypothesis may not extend to non-equiatomic starting conditions.
